chunks: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has an angel in the form of a white rooster. Its head is beneath the Throne, and its feet are in the depths of the seventh earth. It has a wing in the east and a wing in the west. The roosters do not crow until it crows. Then when it crows, it flaps its two wings and then says:
Glory be to Allah, glory be to Allah, glory be to Allah, the Magnificent, the One of whom: “There is nothing like unto Him.”
He said: Then Allah, Blessed and Exalted, answers it and says: “One who knows what you say will not swear falsely by Me.”

key_terms.الْعَرْشِ: the Throne, indicating exalted cosmic rank
key_terms.الْعَظِيمِ: the Magnificent, one of the descriptions of Allah in this passage
key_terms.دِيكٍ: a rooster, here describing the angel’s form
key_terms.سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ: a declaration of Allah’s transcendence and glorification
key_terms.مَلَكًا: an angelic being created by Allah

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith of the angel in the form of a white rooster teach about Allah’s transcendence and truthful oaths?
ai.summary: This hadith describes a cosmic angel in the form of a white rooster whose glorification precedes the crowing of earthly roosters. It emphasizes Allah’s transcendence through the declaration that nothing is like Him, and links awareness of this glorification to truthful reverence when invoking Allah’s Name.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1395 - Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) said:

"Indeed, Allah (swt), Blessed and Exalted, has an angel in the form of a white rooster. Its head is beneath the Throne, and its feet are in the depths of the seventh earth. It has a wing in the east and a wing in the west. The earthly roosters do not crow until this angel crows. When it crows, it flaps its wings and says,
'Glory be to Allah (swt), Glory be to Allah (swt), Glory be to Allah (swt), the Great, who is unlike anything.'

Allah (swt), Blessed and Exalted, responds and says,
'One who knows what you say will not swear falsely by Me.'".
